header.running_head: The Chapter Concerning Da'wah Towards Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ

blocks.text: The Words of Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) Concerning the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah

Hadhrat Abu Bakr (RA) used to say, "There has never been a victory in Islaam greater than the victory at Hudaybiyyah but the people on that day were unable to understand what Muhammad ﷺ and his Rabb were doing. While man is hasty, Allaah does not have the haste man has because of which matters condense to what Allaah has intended. On the occasion of the Farewell Hajj I have seen Suhayl bin Amr standing at the place where animals were being slaughtered, taking Rasulullaah ﷺ's camel closer to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ slaughtered it with his own hand and then called for someone who shaved off his hair. I then saw Suhayl snatching up the hair of Rasulullaah ﷺ and even saw him placing it on his eyes. I then thought that it was the same Suhayl who on the occasion of Hudaybiyyah had refused to allow the writing of بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم and had refused the writing of 'Muhammad the Rasool of Allaah'. I then praised Allaah Who had guided him to Islaam." [^1]
Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) Accepts Islaam

Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) narrates that when they left the trench after the Battle of Ahzaab, he gathered some people from the Quraysh who usually shared his opinions and who did as he said. He said to them, "As you know, I am of the opinion that the Deen of Muhammad shall dominate all others in a very unpleasant manner. However, I see a solution so tell me what you think." When the people asked what he thought, Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) said, "I think that we should join Najaashi (in Abyssinia) and remain there. If Muhammad is victorious, we shall be with Najaashi and being under his rule is better than being under the rule of Muhammad. On the other hand, if our people are victorious, then they would still know us and we can expect only good from them." "This is an excellent opinion," they all agreed. Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) then told them to collect some articles to offer as gifts to Najaashi and because Najaashi liked most the leather from these parts, they collected a large amount of leather. Taking this along, they finally reached Najaashi.
Hadhrat Amr bin Al Aas (RA) narrates further. He says, "By Allaah! We had reached the court of Najaashi when Amr bin Umayyah Damri arrived. Rasulullaah ﷺ had sent him to Najaashi to speak to him about Ja'far (RA) and other Sahabah (RA) (who had migrated to Abyssinia). Amr bin Umayyah entered Najaasjhi's court and then came out again. I said to my companions, 'This is Amr bin Umayyah. If I go to Najaashi and ask request that he (Amr bin Umayyah) be handed over to me so that I could kill him, the Quraysh would feel that I have avenged them by killing the envoy of Rasulullaah ﷺ.' I then entered the court of Najaashi and bowed before him as I always did. He said, 'A hearty welcome to my friend. Have you brought me any gifts from your land?'
